{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Node CI

on: [push]

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x, 20.x, 22.x]

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v1
    - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-node@v1
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
    - name: Cache node modules
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: node_modules
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-node-modules-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-node-modules-
    - name: yarn install, build, and test
      run: |
        yarn install
        yarn test
        yarn build
        yarn test:treeshaking
        yarn test
      env:
        CI: true",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs `yarn install` on every push across a three-version Node matrix, repeatedly fetching dependencies. Evidence pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE shows measured CI workflow savings (20.4% and 6.06% elapsed time) from adding a dependency cache step before installation while keeping all install and test steps intact. Preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching is measurable (push-triggered CI), and cache inputs can include the lockfile. No contraindications apply: no equivalent cache exists, and the cached content is dependency state rather than unchecked build outputs. The change preserves all build and test coverage.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9"]
}
